core_meaning.short_meaning: One who goes in the morning; going, going early
core_meaning.primary_meaning: Ghadi corresponds to the Arabic form غادي and is glossed in this record as “One who goes in the morning; going, going early.” The record associates the form with root غ د و (gh-d-w). The lexical gloss describes the word-form; Qur’anic occurrence, religious recommendation, popularity, and a name-bearer’s character are separate claims and are not established by this gloss alone.
core_meaning.literal_meaning: One who goes in the morning; going, going early
core_meaning.meaning_explanation: Ghadi corresponds to the Arabic form غادي (Arabic root غ د و (gh-d-w); غادي (Ghādī)). Its core sense is swift. Ghadi corresponds to Arabic غادي (Ghādī) 'one who goes in the morning; going, going early', the active participle of the root غ د و (gh-d-w). The source gloss 'swift' is a loose extension. It is used for both sexes in Arabic-speaking countries.
